advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `--repair --dry-run` compute and surface each finding's would-be repair disposition (repairable / unrepairable + reason) without writing any event.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/link_audit.py:285: `if do_repair and not dry_run and findings:` — run_repair (which sets repair_status) is gated off under --dry-run

docstring/AC promise: docs/cli-reference.md:245 `--dry-run   with --repair, preview without writing any event` and the ticket AC '`--repair --dry-run` leaves the event count unchanged while still reporting the findings it would fix'

advisory.finding: `--repair --dry-run` skips run_repair entirely, so no finding is annotated with repair_status/repair_reason — the dry-run output is indistinguishable from a plain scan and never shows which edges would be repaired vs left unrepairable, contradicting the documented 'preview'/'report the findings it would fix' contract.
scenarios: An operator runs `rebar link-audit --repair --dry-run` to see what a repair would do and gets the same list a plain scan produces, with no repairable/unrepairable/ambiguous-pair breakdown.

run_repair (src/rebar/_commands/link_audit.py:223) contains the reconciler-in-flight abort, lock.acquire, and _pre_tag — none reached by the current tests

help text and docs state the exit contract: `exits 1 if anything is found` (src/rebar/_cli/help/link-audit.txt) and `exits 1 while any finding is outstanding, 0 when clean — so it can gate CI` (docs/cli-reference.md)

ABSENCE: no test in tests/scripts/graph/test_link_audit.py invokes `link_audit.link_audit_cli`; the CLI driver in test_schema_coverage.py (`"link-audit": lambda s: ["link-audit"]`, line 108) seeds only sibling/clean tickets via `_seed_for_cli` and asserts JSON shape, never the exit code with an outstanding finding.
advisory.finding: The new test module omits AC-required repair-envelope coverage: there is no `--dry-run` test, no cyclic-replacement `unrepairable` (exit-1) test, and no test of run_repair's safety machinery (reconciler-in-flight abort, write-lock acquisition, pre-link-audit-repair tag OID). The safety-critical --repair envelope is exercised nowhere in the diff.
merged_from: The CLI exit-code contract (`link_audit_cli` returns 1 while findings are outstanding, 0 when clean) — the command's stated CI-gating purpose — is never asserted with findings present. No test calls `link_audit_cli`; the only CLI-level exercise (test_schema_coverage.py's driver) runs on a clean seeded store and validates JSON shape, so a regression flipping the exit logic (e.g. always returning 0, or inverting `1 if outstanding else 0`) would pass every test.
scenarios: A regression in the reconciler-in-flight guard, the lock path, the pre-tag, or the cyclic-decline path would ship undetected.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a repair fault-injection test that raises CommandError (and/or CyclicDependencyError) from the write path and asserts the finding is marked unrepairable with the run continuing.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/link_audit.py:55-60 docstring: `catching ValueError alone would let a real write failure escape and abort the run mid-repair`
src/rebar/_commands/link_audit.py:199: `except _REPAIR_FAULTS as exc:` where `_REPAIR_FAULTS = (ValueError, CyclicDependencyError, CommandError)`
tests/scripts/graph/test_link_audit.py:195-196 and 220-221: both `_boom` helpers `raise ValueError("unlink exploded")` — only the ValueError arm is exercised
src/rebar/_commands/unlink.py:104-107: `_write_unlink` raises `CommandError`, confirming CommandError is a real fault the repair path must catch
advisory.finding: The `_REPAIR_FAULTS` multi-exception catch is regression-blind: the docstring argues catching CommandError and CyclicDependencyError (not just ValueError) is load-bearing because they derive from Exception, not ValueError — yet both fault-injection tests raise only ValueError, so narrowing the catch to `except ValueError` would still pass every test.
advisory.suggested_fix: Duplicate `test_repair_writes_the_replacement_before_removing_the_stale_edge` with `_boom` raising `CommandError` (and one with `CyclicDependencyError`), asserting `repair_status == "unrepairable"` and no dependency lost.
